scope: Per-file contract audit of the final six entries of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt: the X509 trust table and its checkers; X509_certificate_type; the X509_ATTRIBUTE item, constructor and attribute-value printer; the X509_EXTENSION/X509_EXTENSIONS item wrappers; the X509_REQ/X509_REQ_INFO items and the request callbacks, distinguishing-id accessors and library-context helpers; and the X509_CERT_AUX item with the alias/key-id/trust/reject surface.

defects.detail: is_dn_oid returned true for NID_undef, so the V_ASN1_SEQUENCE arm sent every unknown-OID sequence to d2i_X509_NAME. In the exact authority tag (openssl-3.6.4/crypto/x509/x_attrib.c:169-214) the inner switch starts `case NID_undef: /* Unrecognized OID. */ break;`, which exits that inner switch and reaches `return ASN1_parse_dump(...)`; only the nine named attribute types decode a distinguished name. The visible consequence: for an empty Name encoding (`30 00`) the crate printed nothing and answered 0 where the authority dumps and answers positive, and for other bytes it printed `(COULD NOT DECODE DISTINGUISHED NAME)` and answered 0. v3_attrdesc calls the printer with obj_nid 0, so every SEQUENCE algorithm parameter took the wrong arm. Repaired by removing NID_undef from is_dn_oid and correcting the adjacent contract note; a focused regression test pins the DER-dump answer. The line number is the pre-edit locus; is_dn_oid now begins at line 265.

documentation_corrections: src/x509/x_attrib.rs:261-264: the is_dn_oid note claimed NID_undef is attempted as a distinguished name and only falls back to the DER dump when the decode fails. The authority's `case NID_undef: break;` leaves the inner switch for ASN1_parse_dump, so the note now states that only the nine named attribute types take the DN decode and NID_undef takes the dump.
boundary_control: The repaired branch is a compatibility relation, so its control is a differential read of the exact authority tag (openssl-3.6.4/crypto/x509/x_attrib.c:169-214) plus a focused unit test (`x509::x_attrib::tests::undefined_oid_sequence_is_dumped_not_decoded_as_a_name`) that feeds an empty SEQUENCE through an ASN1_TYPE with obj_nid NID_undef and observes a positive answer and a non-empty memory-BIO dump. The old arm answered 0 on the same input.

No C probe exercises ossl_print_attribute_value through v3_aaa/v3_attrdesc/v3_attrmap/v3_sda, so no existing probe transcript changes; the closest probe (RT-STORE) prints basicConstraints and an unknown extension, neither of which reaches the attribute printer.

retained_obligations: src/x509/x509_trust.rs: the reserved rows live in a static UnsafeCell under the authority's unlocked single-threaded table discipline; dynamic rows are CRYPTO_malloc blocks released once by OwnedCtx, and RawTrust releases only the block on the error tail; a row's name is owned only when X509_TRUST_DYNAMIC_NAME is set; X509_TRUST_add's existing-row strdup failure leaves the row with a NULL name and does not free the row, matching the authority's `err: if (idx < 0)` guard; tr_cmp receives pointer-to-element slots; X509_TRUST_cleanup is NULL-tolerant; X509_check_trust's fallback slot is a valid checker and a NULL slot answers 0 instead of reproducing the authority's UB call.

src/x509/x509type.rs: x is live and pkey is NULL-or-live; X509_get0_pubkey may answer NULL and is rechecked; OBJ_find_sigid_algs writes its out-slot only when it answers success; the unit raises nothing.

src/x509/x_attrib.rs: X509_ATTRIBUTE_create takes a static OID by reference, uses the item's empty set stack, and adopts the ASN1_TYPE through ASN1_TYPE_set after a successful push; a failed push releases the attribute and the value exactly once and never the caller's adopted value; the printer requires a live BIO and a live ASN1_TYPE whose selector matches the arm taken; each union arm is read only for its own tag; the DN arm frees its decoded name; print_oid writes into its own 80-byte buffer.

src/x509/x_exten.rs: X509_EXTENSION_free/dup/d2i/i2d and the X509_EXTENSIONS wrapper follow the item layer's allocation, cursor and ownership contract; the embedded OCTET STRING is released by the item destructor, never separately.

src/x509/x_req.rs: pval/exarg obey the item layer's callback contract; rinf_cb installs one empty attribute stack on NEW_POST; req_cb clears distinguishing_id on D2I_PRE/NEW_POST, frees it and the propq member exactly once on FREE_POST, and on DUP_POST copies the context and property query and duplicates the public key, releasing each duplicate once; the GET0 out-slots are writable; the distinguishing-id setter transfers the octet string; ossl_x509_req_set0_libctx is NULL-tolerant and clears propq only through the member-slot token; X509_REQ_new_ex frees the request on a refused context copy.

src/x509/x_x509a.rs: aux_get creates at most one X509_CERT_AUX and answers NULL on refusal; the alias/key-id NULL-name arms clear only an existing string; X509_add1_trust_object accepts a NULL object and answers 1 after aux/stack setup, while X509_add1_reject_object requires a non-NULL object (the authority's own asymmetry); every OBJ_dup product is released exactly once on failure; trust/reject clear use the NULL-tolerant pop_free; the get0 readers borrow the stored alias/key-id data and write len only when it is non-NULL.
